title: Ack and Ack128 are nearly identical - 300 lines of duplication
description:
wire.rs contains two ACK types that differ only in bitmap size:
- Ack<M, N, T> with u64 bitmap (lines 465-640)
- Ack128<M, N, T> with u128 bitmap (lines 645-773)

These structs duplicate:
- Field definitions (rule_id, dtag, window, bitmap, complete)
- `new()` constructor with identical mask logic
- `bitmap_mask()` method
- `write_to()` serialization
- `from_bytes()` parsing

What goes wrong: ~300 lines of near-identical code to maintain. Bug fixes must be applied twice. The Ack128 variant is less tested (no tests use it).

Rewrite options:
1. Use u128 always (no runtime cost on 64-bit, minor on 32-bit)
2. Generic trait `AckBitmap` implemented for u64/u128
3. Macro to generate both
